newsitem.title: USA: Talbots timing shift may hurt April sales.
newsitem.headline: Talbots timing shift may hurt April sales.

text.p: Talbots Inc, reporting higher March sales, said Thursday that sales may have benefited from a shift in timing of its midseason sale, but this shift may hurt April results.

"Our store sales performance in March benefited from the timing shift in our midseason sale, which began one week earlier than the comparable period last year," Chief Executive Arnold B. Zetcher said.

"However, we anticipate that this timing shift will have an adverse impact on April's sales performance. Therefore, the performance of March and April should be viewed together for the most appropriate indication of sales trends.

"On the catalog side," he continued, "sales for the period were softer than expected, which we attribute to a new presentation strategy that emphasized large, impactful displays of key items over our previous strategy of multiple exposures.

"Despite the fact that customers responded well to the merchandise we offered in our recent spring books, because they were given fewer options, our overall sales volume did not reach the levels we had hoped. Therefore, we have moved quickly to correct this issue in our second quarter."

Zetcher added, "Although we are experiencing some timing shifts in our business that will impact our first and second quarters, we have not changed our overall sales outlook for the entire spring season."
